rubric_items.reason: Built on the existing specializations router, the DoctorService private slotStates rule, DoctorRepo, AppointmentRepo.occupyingBetween and the lib helpers. No new infrastructure, no migration, and the route/service/repo layering is kept.

Each story S-1 to S-6 maps to components, and every AC is served: window and PAST rule, the case-insensitive sort with an id tie-break, the unpaged list, 404 and 400, the explicit mapping that keeps out phone, email and patient data, and no change to other routes.

Each EP-1 field has a name, type, nullability, format and example. The 400 message and the 404 status are given exactly, and the start example matches S-1 AC2. The error code values (BAD_REQUEST, NOT_FOUND) are only implied.

Every structural choice is cited or decided by A-03 or A-04, and the code confirms the cited symbols. One trade-off rests on an uncited premise ('the lists are short'), and one sentence puts the Cancelled-appointment filter in the wrong place.

Trade-offs explain why the code sits in DoctorService, why queries run per doctor, why nextSevenDays is left alone, and why fields are mapped one by one instead of returning DoctorSummary. Each line states its cost.

The flow is numbered and clear, and IDs are used the same way throughout the frontmatter and the body. One small inconsistency: new methods are labelled 'changed' while the new type is labelled 'new'.

findings.text: The design says the slot-state rule ignores Cancelled appointments. It does not: slotStates treats any appointment it is given as BOOKED. Cancelled ones are dropped by the SQL in occupyingBetween, so FREE depends on using that exact repo method.

findings.suggested_fix: Say that Cancelled appointments are left out by AppointmentRepo.occupyingBetween, and that earliestSlots must use it (not another appointment query) for S-1 AC4 to hold.

findings.text: The per-doctor query trade-off rests on 'the lists are short', which nothing cites. S-4 AC1 tests more than 20 doctors. The query count also leaves out the refStatus lookup, so the real cost is 2N+2 queries.

findings.text: Impact lists POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/specializations as existing routes on the router this change touches. The design's endpoints list includes only GET /api/specializations, so the regression scope for S-6 is narrower than impact's.
